text:
maria: heads up — eu-central1 NVMe read latency spiked, GPUs failing to attach. seeing attach errors in scheduler logs. ?

sre-bot: ALERT: nodepool/eu-central1-nvme had 90th p99 read latency 320ms over last 5m. affected: gpu-attach, batch-provisioning.

alex: digging into node logs — noticed a fscrypt re-encrypt task started around the same time after a KMS rotation. lots of fscrypt processes scanning scratch mounts.

jamal: who kicked the rotation? coordinated re-encrypts could explain cluster-wide read pressure.

kevin: key-ops ran the scheduled rotation last night. re-encrypt is triggered automatically and should be low-priority, but it looks like it's saturating reads on local NVMe.

maria: sample from gnode-211 /var/log/syslog:
```
Mar 23 02:12:09 gnode-211 fscrypt[4129]: re-encrypt started for /scratch (device /dev/nvme0n1p1)
Mar 23 02:12:11 kernel: nvme 0000:3b:00.0: read latency: 76ms -> 398ms
Mar 23 02:12:41 kubelet: attach failed: ProvisionTimeout
```

alex: confirmed correlation. two immediate mitigation options: pause re-encrypt jobs cluster-wide, or throttle their IO (blkio/systemd IOWeight).

jamal: can we safely pause the re-encrypts? are they required to finish immediately?

kevin: not urgent. re-encrypt is policy-driven. I'll pause the rollout in key-ops but need a way to handle in-flight workers gracefully.

maria: proposed mitigations: 1) set IO caps for fscrypt workers via systemd slice or cgroup2 2) pause remaining scheduled jobs from key-ops controller 3) route new gpu attach requests away from eu-central1 until stable.

alex: tested commands on a node to limit current job IO:
```bash
# limit process IO (example)
eqosctl blkio set 4129 --rw-iops=500 --rw-bps=50M
# or use systemd to lower IO priority for fscrypt
sudo systemctl set-property fscrypt.service IOWeight=10
```

jamal: who can pause the key-ops cron? which service owns that rollout?

kevin: key-ops service owns it; paused the scheduled rollout (confirmed). will also annotate the change to avoid auto-resume.

maria: signalling in-flight fscrypt workers to terminate gracefully (SIGTERM, wait 30s, then SIGKILL if needed). flipping routing policy to prefer us-west2 for new GPU attaches for 15m.

sre-bot: ACTION: key-ops rollout paused (by kevin). in-flight fscrypt workers signalled (maria). routing policy updated: prefer-region us-west2 for new gpu attaches for 15m.

alex: after throttling/killing, p99 read dropped to ~28ms on sampled node. attach retries succeeding.

maria: backlog for GPU attaches cleared for watched queue. schedule: re-encrypt will be rescheduled with IO caps and staged windows during off-peak.

kevin: cost note — routing to us-west2 increased short-term egress/latency costs by ~12%, but prevented SLA breaches. suggestion: preflight check in key-ops to verify fleet IO headroom before triggering bulk re-encrypt.

jamal: +1. add an interlock: only start re-encrypt when average idle IO headroom > threshold and no active attach surges. file follow-up.

maria: creating follow-up ticket INFRA-7893: "KMS-triggered re-encrypt -> IO headroom interlock + throttles" with mitigation steps, playbook, and cost estimate.

kevin: include quick rollback play: pause key-ops + flip route policy + run node-level cgroup caps.

maria: thx — monitoring eu-central1 now. will post updates if anything regresses :white_check_mark:
file_comment: KMS rotation triggered fscrypt re-encrypt tasks that caused NVMe read latency spike and GPU attach failures; thread documents rapid mitigation, commands used, routing fallback, cost note, and follow-up ticket
